scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9058: URGENT!! I can't get through to the far side AT ALL --
from my computer, the machine over there is completely unreachable; every
attempt just dies somewhere in the middle!! Everyone knows our network is two
countries with a border post in the middle where the traffic gets its papers
stamped. Something around the border post must be wrong, but I don't know
what. Could someone look at the box in the middle and get us through -- the
machine over there and I have work to do!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. The OSPF core is converged, R11 redistributes
  between OSPF and EIGRP, and PC0 (20.1.1.x) reaches PC12 (120.1.1.x) with 0% loss
  in both directions. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis of a redistribution / interior-link fault that is not present.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- PC0 cannot reach PC12
across the OSPF/EIGRP core -- is NOT reproducible: the OSPF backbone is converged,
R11 redistributes OSPF<->EIGRP (so the 120.x/EIGRP prefixes appear in the OSPF
RIB and vice versa), and PC0 reaches PC12 (120.1.1.x) with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: cross-core reachability is healthy and
the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the PC0->PC12
path, finds it working, optionally confirms R11's redistribution and the EIGRP
neighbors are up, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a broken
redistribution or a down interior link to satisfy the ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
I verified end-to-end connectivity across the “border post” between the two sites and found no fault. From pc0 (20.1.1.10) to pc12 (120.1.1.10), pings succeeded with 0% loss and ~1.3 ms RTT; the reverse direction also succeeded (~2.3 ms RTT). Traceroutes show clean, symmetric 4-hop paths traversing r1 → r11 → r12 → pc12 and back, with no mid-hop timeouts:
- pc0→pc12: 20.1.1.1 (r1), 111.1.1.2 (r11), 112.1.1.2 (r12), 120.1.1.10
- pc12→pc0: 120.1.1.1 (r12), 112.1.1.1 (r11), 111.1.1.1 (r1), 20.1.1.10
Throughput testing (iperf) from pc0 to pc12 achieved ~63 Mbit/s with 0 retransmissions, indicating a healthy data plane.

At the “border,” r11 (B=111.1.1.2, EE=112.1.1.1) and r12 (EE=112.1.1.2, GG/pc12 LAN=120.1.1.1) are exchanging routes properly: r11’s FRR table shows OSPF toward r1 and EIGRP toward r12; r12 has a default via r11 and directly connected 120.0.0.0/8. Both PCs have correct default gateways (pc0 via 20.1.1.1; pc12 via 120.1.1.1).

Affected component: none (routing, forwarding, and the r11–r12 “checkpoint” are operating normally).
Mechanism: The reported “dies in the middle” symptom would match a border routing/policy break, but tests show stable transit across r11/r12.
Localization: r1 eth4, r11 eth1/eth0, r12 eth0/eth1 on the working path.
Root cause: Not reproducible; no current network fault found.
Corrective fix: No action required. If the issue recurs, capture simultaneous traceroutes from both ends and timestamps to isolate any transient routing or application-layer causes.

The agent's claims are supported by the log outputs (reachability, traceroutes, ifconfig, curl, iperf) and the conclusion (no anomaly) follows directly from those tests; a couple of routing-table details were from truncated outputs but the tool calls exist. Overall the investigation justifies the negative diagnosis.
